newsitem.title: USA: Seitel's Eagle unit files for IPO.
newsitem.headline: Seitel's Eagle unit files for IPO.

text.p: Seitel Inc said Tuesday that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Eagle Geophysical Inc, has filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for the sale of about 73.5 percent of Eagle's common stock in an initial public offering.

About 5,880,000 shares of Eagle will be offered for sale, including four million shares to be offered by Eagle and 1,880,000 shares by Seitel, excluding shares subject to underwriters' over-allotment options.

Upon consummation of the offering, Seitel would continue to own about 19 percent of the outstanding common stock of Eagle, or about 16.5 percent if underwriters' over-allotment options were exercised in full.

Eagle intends to use its net proceeds from the offering to reduce its debt, including about $17 million in debt currently on Seitel's consolidated balance sheet, and to fund planned capital expenditures.
Seitel intends to use its net offering proceeds for general corporate purposes and working capital.

Seitel said it believes that the reduction in Eagle's contribution to Seitel's revenue and earnings as a result of the offering should be more than offset by redeployment of its portion of the offering proceeds to its higher margin seismic data library and petroleum exploration and production businesses.

Eagle, based in Houston, will combine the onshore seismic data acquisition business formerly conducted by Seitel Geophysical and the offshore seismic data acquisition business conducted by Energy Research International (ERI), a Cayman Islands corporation.

Eagle currently owns 19 percent of the outstanding shares of ERI and with consummation of the offering, will acquire the remaining 81 percent of ERI's outstanding shares, in exchange for the issuance of 600,000 shares of Eagle common stock.
